reference: No GNU/POSIX command matches tiv; the loadable inventory lists chafa as missing, and chafa encoding is not a byte-for-byte tiv oracle. These are contract cases, not GNU parity. Help/version expectations follow tiv's documented interface. Rendering expectations use a 2x2 RGB PNG independently encoded from the PNG format (filter-0 scanlines, zlib IDAT, chunk CRCs) with known pixels: top row red/green, bottom row blue/white. The truecolor expectation is computed directly from the documented half-block layout: top pixels become foreground, bottom pixels background, one U+2580 per column, then reset and newline. Inversion complements each known 8-bit channel. File and stdin base64 cases must decode the same independent image bytes.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata and the documented tiv --help and --version output.
Default half-block truecolor rendering for two known vertical pixel pairs at explicit dimensions.
The documented color inversion option over the same image.
PNG input from a base64 file, raw stdin, and base64 stdin.
PTY-dependent sizing and real terminal glyph presentation are recorded as deferred.
exclusions: No matching GNU/POSIX tiv CLI is available, so the suite has no parity cases and does not claim GNU parity.
PTY ioctl dimensions, isatty-dependent width/height fitting, and visual terminal/font behavior require a controlled PTY or terminal emulator and are deferred.
Other color reducers, dense quad/sextant/octant glyphs, malformed-image diagnostics, and broader image formats are not qualified here.

cases.stdout: tiv - Display an image in the terminal (truecolor by default).

cases.purpose: Check the documented version string without invoking image decoding or terminal operations.
Check the complete documented option and format help text emitted by tiv --help.
cases.stdout:
Display an image in the terminal (truecolor by default).

    tiv [OPTION]... FILE

Decodes FILE (PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/TGA; - = stdin) and prints it with block
glyphs. The default half-block glyph shows two vertical pixels per cell;
denser glyphs (-g) pack more detail into the SAME font size by using more
sub-pixels per cell, each cell drawn in two colors (fg/bg).

Options:
    -w, --width N    output width in columns (default: terminal width / 80)
    -H, --height N   output height in terminal rows (default: keep aspect)
    -m, --mode MODE  color: rgb (default) | 256 | ansi | grey | ascii
    -g, --glyph G    density: half (default,1x2) | quad (2x2) | sextant
                     (2x3) | octant (2x4). Denser needs a modern terminal
                     (sextant: Unicode 13; octant: Unicode 16). Ignored for
                     -m ascii.
    -i, --invert     invert colors
        --full       use the full terminal width
        --base64     FILE / stdin holds base64-encoded image data
    -h, --help       show this help
    -V, --version    show version

cases.purpose: Render two known vertical RGB pixel pairs at an explicit 2-column by 1-row size; verify foreground/background ordering, U+2580 cells, reset, and newline.
Verify --invert complements each 8-bit channel while preserving the documented half-block foreground/background layout.
Verify --base64 decodes a base64-encoded PNG file and renders the same independent pixel fixture.
Verify both documented stdin forms: raw PNG from FILE '-' and base64 PNG with --base64 and FILE '-'. Each must render the independently calculated pixels.
Qualify the isatty and TIOCGWINSZ sizing branches with a controlled terminal, including default width, --full width, explicit width, and height-fit behavior.
Qualify how the half, quad, sextant, and octant output appears in a terminal with known Unicode and color support.
